commands.name: lmx
commands.about: Guest owner command of a LimaNix VM

args.name: --help
args.about: Print the guest help page, or the help of the command it follows.

args.name: --version
args.about: Print the version of lmx.

commands.name: lmx help
commands.about: Show the workspace and its commands, or what a module gives you

args.name: TOPIC
args.about: Module to explain, such as `python`, `python-3.12` or `lmx:python-3.12`

commands.name: lmx info
commands.about: Show the kernel, guest disk, shared folders and failed units

commands.name: lmx welcome
commands.about: Show the workspace welcome again

commands.name: lmx status
commands.usage:
lmx status [--json]
lmx status --short
lmx status --wait converged --generation GENERATION [--timeout DURATION] [--json]
commands.about: Show generations, disk usage, network interfaces and failed units
commands.privileges: Nothing. With `sudo` it also reads the generation the Mac selected; `--wait` needs a running `lmxd`

args.name: --short
args.about: Print only what needs attention, such as `restart`, for tmux and the prompt

args.name: --wait

values.name: converged
values.about: The generation is booted, healthy and finalized

args.about: Wait until the guest reaches this state, then answer; the host waits so after a restart. A failed finalize of the generation answers at once

args.name: --generation
args.about: Generation the wait is for

args.name: --timeout
args.about: Longest wait, such as 90s, 10m or 1h [default: 10m]

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

commands.name: lmx doctor
commands.about: Diagnose the configuration, lmxd and the generations, with what to do next
commands.privileges: Nothing. With `sudo` it also reads the generation the Mac selected

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

checks.what: `lmxd` answers, with the same version as `lmx`
The state of the generations, from `lmxd` or, without it, from the generation markers
Shown when `lmxd` reports that the disk is low
Shown when `limanix.toml` names dotfiles: their entries are linked into the home. A `warning` names the paths in the way; `failed` means the directory is not mounted or cannot be read

commands.name: lmx net
commands.about: Check the network inside this VM

commands.name: lmx net check
commands.about: Check why a port of this VM may be unreachable from the Mac: firewall, listener and process
commands.privileges: Nothing. With `sudo` it also sees the processes of other users

args.name: PORT
args.about: Port to check

args.name: --udp
args.about: Check a UDP port instead of a TCP one

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

checks.what: The guest firewall opens the port for its protocol. TCP port 22 is always open for SSH
Something listens on the port, and not only on a loopback address
Which process holds the socket, and which user created it. Only when something listens. Docker's proxy is a warning: `network.ports` does not control the ports Docker publishes

commands.name: lmx logs
commands.about: Show the output of the latest lmxd task of a kind, from the journal
commands.privileges: Root, or membership in the `wheel` or `systemd-journal` group, which may read the journal of `lmxd`

args.name: KIND

values.name: health
values.about: Health checks of the booted generation

values.name: finalize
values.about: Removals of older generations after a healthy boot

args.about: Kind of lmxd task

args.name: --previous
args.about: Read the boot before the running one, such as the one that built the running generation

commands.name: lmx version
commands.about: Show the lmx version and the host contract it speaks

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

commands.name: lmx store
commands.about: Keep room in the Nix store; the work runs in lmxd

commands.name: lmx store reserve
commands.about: Collect unreferenced store paths when free space is low; the host runs it before it stops the VM

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

commands.name: lmx apply
commands.about: Build a requested generation for the next boot; the work runs in lmxd

args.name: --generation
args.about: Generation to apply from its directory under the host's mounted generations

args.name: --follow
args.about: Follow the apply until it ends, with the build's output

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

commands.name: lmx apply cancel
commands.about: Cancel the apply of a generation and wait until it stops

args.name: --generation
args.about: Generation whose apply to cancel

args.name: --json
args.about: Answer with the JSON host contract instead of text

commands.name: lmx clipboard
commands.about: Use the Mac clipboard through the terminal; also installed as pbcopy and pbpaste

commands.name: lmx clipboard copy
commands.about: Copy standard input to the Mac clipboard

commands.name: lmx clipboard paste
commands.about: Print the Mac clipboard, if the terminal allows reads

commands.name: lmx session
commands.about: Open a named session with the selected provider; also installed as limanix-session

args.name: NAME
args.about: Session name, passed to the provider unchanged; put -- before a name that starts with -

commands.name: lmx dotfiles
commands.about: Show which of your dotfiles from the Mac are linked into your home, or link them

commands.name: lmx dotfiles status
commands.about: Show the linked entries, the conflicts and the missing links without changing anything

commands.name: lmx dotfiles link
commands.about: Link the dotfiles into your home; every shell of yours does it as it starts
commands.privileges: The development account. It refuses any other user, root included

args.name: --quiet
args.about: Print nothing but errors, as a starting shell runs it

exit_statuses.what: The command failed, or a check of `lmx doctor` or `lmx net check` failed
`lmxd` is unavailable. Only `store reserve`, `apply`, `apply cancel` and `status --wait` need it
`lmx session` or `limanix-session` found no session provider

environment.what: Set and not empty: no colors

check_statuses.what: Broken. The command exits with status `1`
Your account cannot read what the check needs. Run the command with `sudo`

status_lines.what: The generation the Mac selected (`desired`), the one built for the next boot (`built`) and the one running now (`booted`)
Free space on the disk that holds the Nix store. On a file system with an inode table, free inodes too
Each interface with a global IPv4 address, and its addresses
The version of `lmxd` and what it is doing
What needs attention and why, one line per condition
Why a fact could not be read. That fact shows `unknown`; the other lines still show

short_words.what: The running generation failed its health check
The update works, but removing older generations failed
Less than 10% of the store disk is free
A new generation is built and waits for a restart
An update is being built now
The Mac selected a generation that is not built yet
